review_checks.finding: For every specified scenario the worker checks the Hall neighborhood cardinality condition for every nonempty subset of active unit demands, using each of six distinct unit-capacity slots at most once. For the stated binary eligibility/availability/withholding model this is equivalent to an injective assignment. The logical claim is forall scenarios exists an assignment, not one common fixed allocation across all scenarios.

Six assets and at most three simultaneous demands keep neighborhood counts and thresholds within SecInt(8) bounds. Complete singleton/pair and singleton/pair/triple families contain 21/41 scenarios and 51/191 subset conditions. Loop lengths and public dimensions do not branch on secret values.

Retention is designated asset-specific withholding, not an arbitrary owner reserve quota. Missing eligibility certifies no edge; a false result means declared inputs do not establish the specified allocation, not proof of physical impossibility. Slots must represent distinct assets, eligibility must be correctly established, and demands need exactly one asset.

The cleartext oracle uses backtracking allocation rather than the worker Hall implementation. Structured expected results were independently specified before execution. Bilateral existence ignores simultaneous contention and is explicitly a weak diagnostic, not representative ordinary frontier-model use.

The worker opens one aggregate bit per independent world to all three computing parties and prints the public result only from party 0. It does not open secret edges, neighborhood counts, assignments or per-scenario verdicts. A 120-world research batch authorizes 120 bits, not one bit total. Metadata and the authorized bit itself can leak information with side information.

Execution uses pinned MPyC 0.11, three parties and passive threshold one. This is an honest-majority passive model; local process roles do not establish independent organizations, malicious security, truthful inputs, secure remote channels, ownership or dispatch authority. Public documentation being newer than the pinned execution version is disclosed rather than silently substituted.

Owner-file hashes bind the supplied file bytes and the private schema admits only declared fields and binary matrices with exact dimensions. Hash commitment is not a malicious input proof. Synthetic nonce values are public; production entropy and authenticated channels are outside this component demonstration. The file-open audit hook is an application guard, not operating-system isolation.

Fresh confirmation and ordinary-library replay now require the explicit local --authority fixture. Native role/signature/time and one-use journal checks bind the complete public manifest, input commitments, scenario family, scope/epoch and worker. Temporary raw journal material is deleted and only the public receipt retained. Binding is checked after execution. One-use scope applies within the retained fixture journal; a new temporary journal is not a global privacy budget or rollback-resistant deployment.

The final driver supervises all processes, terminates surviving peers on a nonzero peer or 300-second deadline, collects their bounded worker outputs, writes stdout/stderr and execution.json, and rejects incomplete or failed runs. The --cohort selector separates origin and recipient runs without changing generator or solver semantics. Final source was exercised by this review on both manual scenario families.

Hand-selected deterministic challenges support case-level correctness checks only. Driver Wilson values have been renamed driver_wilson95_inapplicable_for_inference and explicitly marked inapplicable to sampling or population inference. Generator-based intervals, if later reported, concern the synthetic generator; balanced fixed family quotas also warrant approximate/descriptive interpretation rather than a field reliability bound.

An ordinary library receiving the identical artifact and information should tie exactly. Such a tie is expected and must not be represented as retained Alpha or a novel cryptographic algorithm. The diagnostic comparison establishes the value of simultaneous-claim semantics only.
